sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201], but the path was cyclical rather than steady.

The first step change came in FY2017 and FY2018, when revenue rose 18.0% and then 20.4% [D42][D92], driven by higher sales volume from improved end-user demand and favorable dealer inventory changes [P68][P73].
FY2020 reversed that with a 22.4% decline to $41.7 billion [F5][D198], as lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions cut sales across all regions and the three primary segments [P59].

The recovery peaked in FY2023 at $67.1 billion [F8], up 12.8% [D357], on favorable price realization and higher sales volume [P32], before FY2024 fell 3.4% on lower equipment sales to end users [F9][D410][P22].
In FY2025, North America supplied 54.2% of revenue [D513] and contributed 3.4pp of the 4.3% growth [D515][D463], while non-US added just 0.8pp [D540].

The FY2025 increase was primarily higher sales volume of $3.389 billion, partly offset by unfavorable price realization of $817 million [P13], with North America up 6% on higher equipment sales to end users [P12].
Power & Energy was the largest segment at 47.6% of revenue [D757] and contributed 5.2pp of growth [D759], while Construction Industries fell 1.6% and subtracted 0.6pp [D765][D766].
Operating costs grew 4.8pp faster than revenue in FY2025 [D489], at 9.1% [D481], and incremental operating margin was -69.1% [D488].
Diluted EPS fell 14.7% against a 17.7% net income decline [D467][D465], as the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
Operating margin was 16.5% in FY2025 [F30], above the 14.3% window median [D1123] but below the 20.2% FY2024 high [D1122] and well above the 3.0% FY2016 low [D1121].

The 3.7pp operating-margin decline in FY2025 [D476] came mostly from cost of revenue, a -4.2pp effect [D490], as unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion largely reflected higher tariffs [P9].

The largest positive move was FY2023, when operating margin rose 6.0pp [D370] on a +5.8pp cost-of-revenue effect [D384], helped by favorable price realization and the absence of the 2022 goodwill impairment [P31].
In FY2025 net margin of 13.1% sat 3.4pp below the 16.5% operating margin [F50][F30][D1168], with the 24.0% effective tax rate [D449] and $892 million of other income [X110] bridging the gap.
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income in FY2025 [F80][F40][D450], above the 1.16x window median [D1158], and free cash flow covered net income at 1.00x [D451].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow rose to $12.278 billion from $11.437 billion [P4], primarily on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid [P4].
Free cash flow margin was 13.2% [D447], below the 16.8% FY2023 high [D1128], as capex rose 41.9% to $2.821 billion [D470][F90], 4.2% of revenue [D446] and 1.25x D&A [D452].
Days inventory outstanding was 148 days [D461] and days sales outstanding 59 days [D460], both above their FY2023 levels of 141 and 51 days [D355][D354].
Cash and investments of $9.980 billion against total debt of $36.210 billion left net debt of $26.230 billion in FY2025 [D454][D455][D456], or net cash of -38.8% of revenue [D457].

That net cash level ranked at the 67th percentile of three industrials peers, against a -59.4% peer median [D1169][D1170], though total debt omits long-term debt due within one year, $7.1 billion in FY2025 [R7].
Buybacks of $5.190 billion and dividends of $2.749 billion [X140][X150] were 89.0% of free cash flow [D459], and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [D483].
Return on average equity was 43.5% [D462], at the 100th percentile of six industrials peers against a 23.3% median [D1155][D1156].
Long-term debt due within one year sits in no line of this pack across FY2016-FY2025, running from $5.3 billion to $9.1 billion a year and $7.1 billion in FY2025 [R7][X180][D455].
Total debt and net cash therefore understate leverage, so the 67th-percentile net cash ranking should be read with that omission in mind [R7][D1169].
Net debt rose for a second year through FY2025 [R1][D350][D403][D456], and revenue declined 3.4% in FY2024 [R2][F9][D410].
The FY2024 dip was a volume-driven pause rather than a structural break, since FY2025 revenue recovered to $67.6 billion [F10][P22].
Net income for FY2021-FY2025 in the metrics table comes from the proxy statement's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, differing by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20].
The gap is immaterial to margins and cash conversion, but the 10-K figure is the one to cite where precision matters [R3].
If FY2026 operating margin falls below the 14.3% window median [D1123], the FY2025 tariff-driven cost pressure would be confirmed as persistent, visible in the FY2026 10-K.

If free cash flow margin drops below the 11.9% window median [D1129] from 13.2% [D447], the capex step-up to 4.2% of revenue [D446] would be weighing on conversion, reported in the FY2026 cash flow statement.
If net cash as a share of revenue falls below the -38.8% FY2025 level [D457], leverage would be rising further, disclosed in the FY2026 balance sheet.
